lines.trans: He put me in charge of the Variety Department sports day? Think that is a menial chore? Far from it!
Sports day is the first litmus test gauging how popular the new director actually is inside Variety.
Fifty people turned out under Director Choi last year—our target this year is eighty!
I hate running and find moving around a hassle in general—the only joy of sports day is eating!
The fun of eating the catered buffet together—there is always roast wild-boar pork and cold beer!
We are already dead tired, yet everyone herds around playing basketball and soccer—we do it every year and I hate it.
Honestly, for the first time since joining KBS, I thought: what a wonderful workplace this is!
Charging toward a shared goal alongside my seniors, I felt the true joy of togetherness.
Once a year honestly feels way too rare—I wish we held sports day every single quarter!

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.
Let's go together.
Let's go together. (2)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: The fun of eating the catered buffet together—there is always roast wild-boar pork and cold beer!

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'is the place' is key.

examples.text: 장기간 햇빛을 못 보니까 팀 차원에서 비타민 D를 공동 구매하기 시작했죠, 살아보겠다고.
examples.trans: Because we go so long without sunlight, our whole team started group-buying vitamin D just to stay alive.

examples.text: 뛰는 것도 싫고 원래 움직이는 것 자체를 귀찮아하는 편이라 체육대회를 무슨 낙으로 오냐, 먹는 거지!
examples.trans: I hate running and find moving around a hassle in general—the only joy of sports day is eating!

examples.text: 선배님들과 함께 공동의 목표를 향해 다 같이 함께하는 기쁨을 느꼈습니다.
examples.trans: Charging toward a shared goal alongside my seniors, I felt the true joy of togetherness.

examples.text: 어떻게 보면 불쌍하지, 낙이 없으니까 그렇게 토너에 집착하는 거지.
examples.trans: In a way it is sad—having no other joy in life is why she obsesses over toner like that.

examples.text: 나 십 년 동안 시키는 대로 다 했잖아요.
examples.trans: For ten years, I did everything you told me to do.

examples.text: 이십 년 넘게 친구 설정으로 지냈는데 쉽진 않겠지.
examples.trans: You lived as friends for over twenty years, so changing that won't be easy.

examples.text: 이렇게 피곤해 죽겠는데 우르르 몰려다니면서 농구하고 축구하고, 매년 하는 거지만 싫죠.
examples.trans: We are already dead tired, yet everyone herds around playing basketball and soccer—we do it every year and I hate it.

examples.trans: I noticed this last time too—who do you think you are lecturing about romance?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 느끼다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (felt, noticed).

examples.text: 걱정은 하지, 늘. 근데 왜 백승찬을 집에 자꾸 들이냐?
examples.trans: I always worry. Still, why do you keep letting Baek Seung-chan into the house?

examples.text: 늘 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (always), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.

meanings.note: Also used for jumping or a heart beating fast.

examples.trans: Why are you running?

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.

examples.text: 우리 예능국 체육대회를 맡겼다고? 이게 잡무 같지? 아니다 이거!
